Values and sources

EPA/O means expected points added per included quarterback play. D means recorded dropbacks; O includes those dropbacks and non-scramble quarterback runs. It is not a percentile interval, every source of uncertainty or a test of the difference between players.

How the model works

The seven clockwise positions address arm strength, a processing proxy, pocket presence, mobility, short accuracy, medium accuracy and deep accuracy. The default Mahomes–Allen comparison combines two expert assessments published before the 2023 season with five outcomes from the 2023 regular season. These are different evidence types and observation windows. Other player-years retain their available outcomes and explicit expert gaps; no rank carries into another year.

Method

Attribute profile: two scales, sources and limits

Dropbacks without a sack (%) occupies the desired pocket-presence position. Scramble contribution occupies the desired mobility position using the separate annual Mobility export: 559 finite accepted points among 560 qualifying player-seasons. Kyle Boller 2007 is withheld pending recorded-role review; 2011 is excluded. Sack avoidance reflects protection, receiver availability and decisions with other costs. Scramble contribution combines usage with whole-play shared value. Neither isolates the desired trait.

The short, medium and deep positions show completions above expectation on throws in each depth bin, in percentage points. These depth-specific completion residuals describe recorded outcomes relative to the supplied model; they do not isolate throwing accuracy or ball placement. Read the depth bins and formula.

Each percentile describes where a recorded outcome sits among its fixed same-year peers. For dropbacks without a sack and each of the three depth outcomes, peers are that year’s qualifying passers with a finite value for that outcome. Annual qualification requires at least 200 included throws across at least 10 included-throw games; depth bins add no minimum throw-count rule. Peer membership comes from the validated source records and cannot change with the selected opponent or search text. Each available outcome shows its year and peer count, N.

Annual Mobility percentiles use finite accepted scramble contributions from the qualifying player-seasons in that year. The 2007 pool has 26 values because the Boller point is withheld; 2023 has 29 and 2024 has 32. These are separate from the 20-QB pools used for the repeatability study. Each of the other four outcomes uses its own comparison pool. Compare each stat’s displayed year and finite peer count.

The midpoint-percentile formula is P = 100 × (B + 0.5 × T) / N. Here B counts peer values below the selected value, T counts exact ties including the selected record, and N counts all finite peer values including that record. Ties use unrounded native values. Higher recorded outcomes receive higher percentiles on all five measured spokes. A constant finite cohort gives every record 50; fewer than two peers or an unavailable native value gives no percentile. Missing evidence never becomes zero or 50, and another season never supplies a replacement.

The five outcome spokes use radius P / 100; 50 describes midpoint standing, not a zero native outcome or average ability. The two expert spokes instead use the ordinal drawing index (11 - rank) / 10: rank #1 is outer and #10 is at one-tenth radius. This index is not an NFL percentile or a calibrated ability grade. Numeric ring labels are omitted because the two scales have different meanings. Whole-number labels round half up using floor(P + 0.5); geometry retains the full percentile. Endpoints are not stretched to force a 1 or 100. With 20 untied peers, percentiles run from 2.5 to 97.5 in five-point steps. Whole-number labels do not imply one-point skill resolution.

Farther out means higher same-year standing on that outcome. Cross-year comparisons use different reference cohorts; they do not establish absolute ability or trait improvement. Equal percentile gaps need not mean equal differences in native outcomes or ability. The three depth outcomes share context and correlated evidence, so they do not count as three independent skill votes. Compare one spoke at a time: no area, aggregate score or winner combines them. Lines join adjacent available positions only. No line bridges a gap. The final edge closes only when all seven positions are available; the shape has no fill.

Optional full evidence retains raw values, counts and native-unit conditional game-based ranges. Those raw ranges are not percentile confidence intervals. They do not form a joint confidence region, predict performance or test a player/year difference. Individual sack-avoidance uncertainty was not estimated. The negative-depth diagnostic remains outside the radar. Read the range assumptions, the play populations, the sack formula, and the scramble formula.

Expert assessments: source, coverage and measurement limits

The data contain 84 published ESPN rank facts for same-year annual-eligible quarterbacks in the 2021–2025 preseason editions: 41 arm-strength ranks, 26 field-vision ranks and 17 decision-making ranks. Missing or unlisted entries remain unavailable; they do not mean last, low ability or an inferred rank. The source rank label, tie and marker are retained.

Processing uses field vision in 2021–2023 and decision-making with the football in 2024–2025. Each is a different partial editorial assessment, not measured thinking speed or a complete decision-quality grade. The selected values show the actual category, preseason edition, source date and panel or individual author. Different editions, categories and authorship do not form a comparable skill time series. A rank difference does not measure improvement. The expert axes use ordinal drawing indices, not outcome percentiles; equal rank steps do not establish equal skill gaps. Source uncertainty remains unquantified.

  • ESPN 2021 preseason edition · 2021-08-23: NFL experts; Panel; individual and joint contributor slots. Points combined from personal top-ten ballots; weights not specified.
  • ESPN 2022 preseason edition · 2022-08-22: NFL Experts; Panel; individual and joint contributor slots. Points combined from personal top-ten ballots; weights not specified.
  • ESPN 2023 preseason edition · 2023-08-14: NFL experts; Nine named analysts. Points combined from personal top-ten ballots; weights not specified.
  • ESPN 2024 preseason edition · 2024-08-12: Dan Orlovsky; Individual judgment. Current performance and upcoming-season expectations; article uses tape observations.
  • ESPN 2025 preseason edition · 2025-08-11: Dan Orlovsky; Individual judgment. Current performance and upcoming-season expectations; tape-based; starters only.

Comparable isolated arm strength would need calibrated ball-speed observations and throw geometry. Processing would need validated observations of available options and choices. Those measurements remain unavailable. The sourced judgments supply a distinct kind of evidence; they do not establish those missing measurements. No expert confidence interval or composite score is invented.

How the models work

The data provider supplies completion chances and expected-points values. This project summarizes recorded outcomes using those values. The fixed-cohort studies examine associations across game groups and seasons; the wider annual and depth data provide descriptive comparisons.

The supplied completion model uses recorded throw/context information. The inspected upstream implementation includes depth/location, down/distance and a QB-hit field; these are not all independent of QB decisions. The project neither fits nor retrains this model. The supplied data do not identify which model or training sample generated these values, their out-of-sample status or their calibration in each era. Completion model implementation.

The upstream expected-points model uses game-state inputs such as field position, down/distance and time left. It estimates scoring-event probabilities and converts them to expected points. EPA then values the resulting play. The project uses supplied raw EPA, not receiver-fumble-adjusted QB EPA, and fits no expected-points model. The generating expected-points model and training vintage remain unknown for these snapshots. Modeled game-state adjustment does not isolate protection, receivers or coaching. Comparing seasons with different football conditions and unknown model calibration does not produce an era-neutral ability comparison. Official expected-points explanation · EPA implementation.

What the game-based ranges mean

An approximate range based on game-to-game variation, under the study’s assumptions. Here, the bars describe approximate uncertainty around each summary, not the spread of game performances. These conditional ranges are not probabilities for true talent, predictions for next season or bounds on every source of uncertainty.

The annual EPA range removes one complete player dropback game at a time and recalculates the pooled EPA/dropback ratio, holding qualification fixed. It uses all games containing that player’s recorded dropbacks. The run-contribution ranges for the 20-passer study use all combined-opportunity games, including games with zero events of the named run role.

Depth ranges use all of the player’s included-throw games in that season, including games with zero throws in the named depth bin. Let G be that full game count, n_bg the bin throws in game g, and s_bg their sum of supplied CPOE values. The full estimate is theta_b = sum_g(s_bg) / sum_g(n_bg). The leave-one-game-out estimate is theta_b[-g] = (sum_h(s_bh) − s_bg) / (N_b − n_bg). A zero-bin game remains a deletion with no removed bin throws; the positive-bin-game count does not replace G.

Every deletion must retain a positive denominator and finite estimate. The analysis neither drops failed replicates nor requalifies the player after deletion. An empty bin leaves the estimate unavailable; an invalid deletion leaves the range unavailable, with an explicit status. For valid deletions, m = sum_g(theta[-g]) / G, V = (G−1)/G × sum_g((theta[-g]−m)^2), and the displayed range is theta ± 1.96 × sqrt(V). This is an approximate marginal 95% conditional game-deletion sensitivity, not the minimum-to-maximum deletion range.

A collapsed range means no observed deletion variation, not certainty. Whole-season CPOE, completion rate and individual sack avoidance have no supplied individual range here. The three depth ranges do not provide simultaneous 95% coverage. Marginal ranges neither test differences between depth bins, players or years nor establish rank certainty; overlap and non-overlap do not supply those missing tests.

The calculation assumes approximately independent game shocks, stable opportunity sampling and a useful normal approximation, conditional on fixed qualification and observed support. It omits uncertainty from selection, serial injuries, receivers, protection, coverage, scheme, source labels and the supplied models’ training/calibration. Unknown model vintage and era changes preclude talent-confidence, causal, era-neutral or forecasting interpretations.

Formulas

CPOE = completion percentage − expected completion percentage.

EPA = value of the result − expected points before the play.

Without a sack (%) = 100 × (dropbacks − sacks) ÷ dropbacks.

Signed scramble contribution is C_S = sum(raw supplied EPA on recorded scrambles) / N_O, in expected points per included recorded quarterback play. It combines scramble usage with shared whole-play value. It does not measure speed, all rushing ability or isolated mobility. A fully observed zero-scramble role with positive O gives a genuine zero contribution. There are four such rows; zero does not mean zero mobility talent. Positive and negative EPA can also cancel.

Formulas: C_S = sum_S(EPA)/N_O; C_R = sum_R(EPA)/N_O. Shares are 100 × N_S/N_O and 100 × N_R/N_O, percent. EPA per run divides each role’s EPA by that role’s count and remains a diagnostic with no supplied interval or repeatability test. A fully observed absent role has zero share and contribution, with unavailable per-run EPA. Zero contribution can also result from positive and negative EPA cancelling; inspect the counts. Missing evidence never becomes zero. Adding these contributions to EPA per dropback would mix denominators and double-count scrambles.

Correlation is r = sum_i[(x_i−mean(x)) × (y_i−mean(y))] / sqrt(sum_i(x_i−mean(x))² × sum_i(y_i−mean(y))²) across equally weighted passers. Their pooled summaries supply x/y. Near +1 means strong positive linear alignment, not identical values. Zero means no linear association, not zero talent. Constant values make correlation undefined.

Validation and research

Research question

How do quarterbacks compare when we isolate them from their team and situation?

What repeatability measures

The findings below belong to the fixed 20-passer 2023/2024 cohort and its ten study records. The 560-player-season annual data and depth summaries do not establish repeatability for that broader sample.

Repeatability asks whether players with higher values in one group also tended to have higher values in the other. Across-passer association does not measure a selected player’s personal consistency, absolute agreement, retained-skill percentage or forecast accuracy.

The sack study’s 2023 halves alternate each player’s date/game-ID-ordered dropback games; run halves alternate combined-opportunity games. Whole player-games stay intact. Annual comparisons use full 2023/2024 summaries. These shared/overlapping studies are not independent replications and do not directly test future performance.

Annual CPOE association was 0.507, versus 0.452 for completion percentage on the same throws. Their difference was 0.055, with a conditional interval from −0.274 to 0.384. Omitting one paired player reverses that difference. The evidence does not establish CPOE superiority. The paired correlation difference is dimensionless, not a percentage-point completion gap.

Recorded sack avoidance had a primary interleaved association of 0.265 [−0.289,0.685]. Chronological and annual results answer separate questions; all three remain in the study table.

Primary scramble-contribution association was 0.313 [−0.190,0.686]; other-run association was 0.697 [0.004,0.938]. Annual associations were 0.727 [0.226,0.924] and 0.429 [−0.080,0.761]. All four endpoints remain in the study table.

Study ranges remove a whole contributing NFL game across both teams and selected players, keeping membership/maps fixed. Sack/run correlations use Fisher transforms and each season’s own deletion mean. Annual CPOE retains its accepted full-estimate centering; the paired difference uses the same game deletions for both metrics. These approximate conditional ranges assume approximately independent game shocks and suitable smooth-statistic behavior. The 223 + 208 annual game units do not form 431 independent quarterback pairs or repeated validation studies.

Limitations

What these comparisons cannot tell us

Receiver/defender actions, target choices and unmeasured circumstances remain. Protection, receivers and coaching are not isolated. These summaries do not establish precise placement, pocket awareness, designed rushing, athletic mobility, overall QB quality or forecasts. Isolated arm-strength and processing measurements and a support-adjusted overall score remain unavailable; the profile separately identifies its limited preseason expert assessments.

The annual display exports qualifying records from 2006–2025, excluding 2011 because of unresolved source conflicts. Eligibility selects for recorded exposure and completion-model availability, and the repeatability study requires qualification in both years. Source coverage, overlap, persistent support and conditional uncertainty limit interpretation. Unknown generating model vintages and era changes prevent era-neutral skill claims. The depth residuals share outcomes and context; they do not validate three isolated accuracy traits. Percentiles describe standing within each declared outcome/year cohort. No aggregate percentile, win count or blended score combines the radar spokes or optional comparisons.

Definitions

Value per dropback

Average EPA on this player’s recorded passes, sacks and scrambles.

Unit: expected points per recorded dropback. Positive means modeled improvement over the starting situations, not proof of above-league-average or independent QB ability.

Value per dropback = sum of dropback EPA ÷ number of recorded dropbacks.

The formula is sum_D(epa_t)/N_D. Total EPA is the numerator alone; efficiency and volume answer different questions. Read which plays count, how expected points work, and the limitations.

Completions above expectation (CPOE)

How far the player’s completion rate finished above or below the model’s expectation for the included throws.

Unit: percentage points. The supplied play value is 100 × (recorded completion − supplied completion probability). The project averages those supplied values across the same included throws used for completion rate. In symbols: mean_E(cpoe_t) = 100 × sum_E(y_t − p_t) / N_E, where y_t is one for a completion and zero otherwise, and p_t is the supplied probability between zero and one. The expected completion rate explains CPOE; it is not an additional player metric.

Zero means matching that model expectation on the included throws, not zero accuracy. Receiver/defender actions, target choices and unmeasured circumstances remain. This does not measure ball placement or all-around accuracy. Model explanation · Included throws · Limitations.

Completions above expectation by throw depth

Air yards measure the recorded target depth relative to the line of scrimmage. The short bin includes throws from 0 up to, but not including, 10 air yards: [0,10). Medium uses [10,20) and deep uses [20,70). The separate negative-air-yard bin uses [−15,0) and remains an optional diagnostic, outside the radar. Boundaries belong to the bin starting at that value; a throw at 10 air yards is medium. These bins do not identify read order, target openness, arm strength or processing.

For a bin b, let E_b contain that player’s included throws in that season and bin, with N_b throws. Its completion residual is theta_b = mean_E_b(cpoe_t) = 100 × sum_E_b(y_t − p_t) / N_b. Here y_t is one for a recorded completion and zero otherwise, and p_t is the supplied completion probability. This is a pooled throw-level mean, not an average of game percentages. A value of +3 percentage points means the observed completion rate exceeded the model’s expectation by three points on those bin throws.

The annual eligibility threshold applies before depth splitting; the analysis adds no minimum bin-volume rule. Evidence shows the bin’s throw count, games containing bin throws, and all included-throw games. An empty bin has no estimate. A failed game-deletion denominator leaves its range unavailable; no failed deletion disappears from the calculation and no unavailable value becomes zero. Read the game-based calculation.

Percentage points

Percentage points are differences between percentages, not percent improvement or a percentile. CPOE subtracts the expected completion percentage from the observed completion percentage on the same throws.

Completion rate

The percentage of included throws recorded as complete. It uses the same eligible throws as CPOE here, not every official passing attempt. Formula: 100 × recorded completions / included throws. It remains a diagnostic comparator in the optional research.

Expected completion chance (CP)

The supplied model’s estimated chance that an included throw becomes a completion. Recorded throw context explains some difficulty; the estimate does not measure throwing talent or every influence on the play. CP supplies explanatory background, not another player metric.

Expected points

The model’s value of a game situation, based on chances of the next scoring event in the half. Values are signed from the team-with-possession perspective. This is a model expectation, not a promised score.

Formula: EP(x) = sum_j[p_j(x) × v_j], where p_j is the upstream probability of a scoring category and v_j its signed scoring value, including zero for no score. How the supplied models work.

Play value (EPA)

How much a play improved or worsened the offense’s expected points. Expected points added is whole-play shared value, not points personally created by the QB or actual points scored.

The provider values the result after scoring, possession and period-ending handling. On an ordinary non-scoring play with continuing possession within a half, this reduces to expected points after minus expected points before. Turnovers require the original offense’s perspective; scoring and end-of-half cases require the provider’s rules. The project uses supplied EPA and does not rebuild it by subtracting consecutive play-by-play rows. Zero EPA means no modeled net gain, not zero yards or no scoring. Model explanation · Limitations.

Dropbacks without a sack

The percentage of recorded dropbacks that did not end in a recorded sack.

The denominator is recorded dropbacks, not pressures or included throws. Interceptions, incompletions and low-value escapes can count as avoiding a sack. Protection and receiver availability matter. This is not measured pressure escape or pocket presence. Individual uncertainty was not estimated. Play definitions · Limitations.

Who and which plays are included?

The denominator is the count you divide by; it determines which plays the statistic describes.

Annual eligibility and source coverage

The annual comparison contains 560 qualifying player-seasons across 19 exported seasons from 2006 through 2025. Each player qualifies within that season with at least 200 frozen included throws and ten included-throw games. Team changes pool under the same recorded GSIS player ID. No adjacent-season appearance is required. These are recorded passers, not a position-certified roster or every NFL quarterback; completion-model availability and exposure affect who qualifies. The postseason is excluded.

The catalog retains all 20 years. 2011 is excluded because unresolved duplicate recorded events and conflicting air yards prevent an accepted input. It contributes no annual or depth rows. Years outside 2006–2025 have no accepted data in this comparison. A selected player-year without an eligible record stays unavailable; the display does not substitute a nearby year, another player or zero.

The repeatability evidence uses a separate, fixed group of 20 surviving passer IDs with at least 200 included throws and ten included-throw games in both 2023 and 2024. The study contains 40 annual records and ten study records. Those repeatability findings do not describe the full set of 560 player-seasons. The profile’s annual Mobility values describe the annual comparison sample, separate from the 40-record repeatability study.

  • Included throws (E): the accepted recorded pass-outcome population, with finite supplied completion probability and CPOE, completion probability between zero and one, air yards at least −15 and below 70, observed pass location and the accepted receiver-name or receiver-ID condition. Frozen eligibility checks the CPOE identity. CPOE and completion share these exact rows; there is no FTN filter or missing-as-zero rule. The public audit code specifies the full pass-outcome/key rules.
  • Recorded dropbacks (D): recorded dropbacks on pass/run play types, with spike, kneel and two-point flags zero. Passes/sacks use the raw passer ID; scramble-runs use the raw rusher ID. Played penalties remain. Other play types and no-play records lie outside this population. It has no completion, completion-probability or included-throw-game filter, and may differ from another site’s dropback rule.
  • Scrambles (S): the recorded scramble-run subset of dropbacks. These counts describe opportunities, not pressures escaped.
  • Other recorded runs (R): recorded non-scramble runs by an eligible actor ID, excluding kneels and conversions. The annual Mobility export applies this definition independently by year; the repeatability study uses its separate fixed group. They include aborted plays and laterals. Non-scramble does not establish designed-run intent or athletic mobility.
  • Included recorded QB plays (O): the disjoint union of recorded dropbacks and other recorded runs. Scrambles already belong to dropbacks. This is a selected recorded-opportunity population, not every snap or offensive play.

Games count distinct player games containing the named type of record. Role games contain at least one event of that run type. Summed player-game counts are not distinct NFL games. Full audit and reproduction code.

Annual scramble contribution

The annual Mobility export uses the frozen 560 qualifying player-seasons, without requiring an adjacent-season appearance. It does not add a performance, positive-EPA, completion-probability or included-throw-game filter to the running plays. Recorded dropbacks follow AD-1.1; other runs follow the accepted recorded-run definition. The disjoint denominator is N_O = N_D + N_R; scrambles already belong to dropbacks. R-only games and games with no scrambles remain included.

Kyle Boller 2007 has retained counts but a null point and range pending review of a contradictory recorded role with missing EPA. The export does not repair the source, drop that event or assign zero. There are 559 finite accepted points. The 2007 finite reference N is 26; 2011 has no invented rows. Each profile percentile uses the same OP-1.0 midpoint rule on its fixed same-year finite annual Mobility pool, including the focal record and exact raw-value ties. Search, opponent and checkbox choices cannot change that pool.

Approximate marginal ranges use all-O-game deletion sensitivity, including zero-scramble and R-only games, under the working assumptions. A collapsed zero range means no observed deletion variation, not certainty. These conditional ranges omit other uncertainty sources, do not predict ability or performance, and do not test differences between the selected players or years. The 40-record running study uses separate 20-QB percentile pools.

Running values in the repeatability study

These running summaries cover the 40 audited records in the 2023/2024 repeatability study. The profile uses the separately validated annual Mobility export described above. Neither source substitutes scramble rate or dropbacks for an uncalculated contribution, and the annual comparison sample does not support broader repeatability conclusions.

Value from scrambles is scramble EPA spread over all included dropbacks and other recorded player runs. Other recorded run value spreads non-scramble-run EPA over those same included plays. These contributions combine usage with shared value; more usage is not universally better.
